body:
I've tried a similar situation now on my Mac and no error is printed 🤔 

- Same build: `v4.4.beta3.official [06acfccf8]`
- Different system: `Godot v4.4.beta3 - macOS Sequoia (15.3.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M2 (Apple8) - Apple M2 (8 threads)`

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a9d96f0-fb43-4516-aa6e-97425f274a94)

Now I'm thinking either it's the RigidBody3D (very weird) or just Windows (very likely) messing around

I had a similar thing happen, and I discovered that a MeshInstance3D had the "skeleton" property set somehow (I never set one). I clicked the "reset" button on that property to clear it and now it no longer shows the "node not found" error message upon loading the project 🎊 

I think the "skeleton" property of my mesh may have gotten changed when I re-parented a node that it's a descendant of...? So maybe there is a bug here

v4.4.beta3.official [06acfccf8] (on Linux)

> I had a similar thing happen, and I discovered that a MeshInstance3D had the "skeleton" property set somehow (I never set one). I clicked the "reset" button on that property to clear it and now it no longer shows the "node not found" error message upon loading the project 🎊
> 
> I think the "skeleton" property of my mesh may have gotten changed when I re-parented a node that it's a descendant of...? So maybe there is a bug here

I had exactly the same issue. I re-parented a MeshInstance3D to a Node3D and I also extracted to new Scene. The value of the skeleton property was messed up.

 v4.4.rc2.official [01545c995] on Linux

The assignment of the `skeleton` property happens in the `EditorUndoRedoManager::commit_action` method here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4c311cbee68c0b66ff8ebb8b0defdd9979dd2a41/editor/scene_tree_dock.cpp#L3084

But I'm struggling a little bit with debugging. I'm using CLion and can't see all the NodePaths and StringNames in the debugger right away.

The `skeleton_path` seems to have `..` (= parent) as a default value. And when reparenting the mesh instance (I just drag it in the tree), it updates the path so that it's still pointing to the same node! 

It's really strange that the `skeleton_path` gets assigned such a strange value when _reparenting to new node_ specifically. My debug print: (the scene root is named "World")

```txt
old: skeleton_path: '..'
new: p_skeleton: '../../root/@EditorNode@21278/@Panel@14/@VBoxContainer@15/DockHSplitLeftL/DockHSplitLeftR/DockHSplitMain/@VBoxContainer@26/DockVSplitCenter/@VSplitContainer@54/@VBoxContainer@55/@EditorMainScreen@102/MainScreen/@CanvasItemEditor@11488/@VSplitContainer@11140/@HSplitContainer@11142/@HSplitContainer@11144/@Control@11145/@SubViewportContainer@11146/@SubViewport@11147/World'
```

I have the same error dangling in editor output and play mode debugger. ``` E 0:00:00:897 get_node: Node not found: "../../root/@EditorNode@21272/@Panel@14/@VBoxContainer@15/DockHSplitLeftL/DockHSplitLeftR/DockHSplitMain/@VBoxContainer@26/DockVSplitCenter/@VSplitContainer@54/@VBoxContainer@55/@EditorMainScreen@102/MainScreen/@CanvasItemEditor@11482/@VSplitContainer@11134/@HSplitContainer@11136/@HSplitContainer@11138/@Control@11139/@SubViewportContainer@11140/@SubViewport@11141/Node3D" (relative to "/root/main_test/Level/Floor"). Method/function failed. Returning: nullptr scene/main/node.cpp:1877 @ get_node() ``` But mine appeared after I reparented multiple nodes (using "Reparent to New Node...") and now it appears every time I start the game (my project was created yesterday and not converted from an older Godot version). The "Floor" is just a static mesh of a built-in plane. But for some reason after reparenting it Godot decided to add a skeleton to it? The scene looked like this before: ``` [node name="Floor" type="MeshInstance3D" parent="."] mesh = SubResource("QuadMesh_fodur") ``` And this is after: ``` [node name="Floor" type="MeshInstance3D" parent="Level"] mesh = SubResource("QuadMesh_fodur") skeleton = NodePath("../../root/@EditorNode@21272/@Panel@14/@VBoxContainer@15/DockHSplitLeftL/DockHSplitLeftR/DockHSplitMain/@VBoxContainer@26/DockVSplitCenter/@VSplitContainer@54/@VBoxContainer@55/@EditorMainScreen@102/MainScreen/@CanvasItemEditor@11482/@VSplitContainer@11134/@HSplitContainer@11136/@HSplitContainer@11138/@Control@11139/@SubViewportContainer@11140/@SubViewport@11141/Node3D") ``` > Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6119) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600H with Radeon Graphics (12 threads)
